title: Server-authoritative bomb passing
prompt: Build a multiplayer hot-potato mechanic with an 8-second fuse. For a multiplayer round, wait for at least two players to join; once that joined set has remained unchanged for 2 seconds, the server assigns the first bomb to the joined player with the lowest UserId. A new join restarts the stability timer. To support solo play before a round has begun, start a solo round after a 12-second single-player grace period. The holder presses E to pass it to the nearest player within 12 studs, the fuse keeps its original deadline across passes, and expiration deals 40 damage to the current holder exactly once. Ignore client-supplied player identities. If the holder disconnects, clear ownership and return to a waiting state. Clearly communicate ownership and remaining danger without obscuring play.
acceptance: For two or more joined players, a 2-second stable join window precedes initial assignment to the lowest-UserId player; a new join restarts that window. A sole player receives a 12-second grace period before solo assignment. The server owns range validation, the 8-second fuse, damage, cleanup, and disconnect recovery.
A real E key press passes to the nearby player, while out-of-range and forged requests leave ownership unchanged.
Passing preserves one fuse deadline; expiration damages the current holder once and records one explosion.
Both clients converge on the server-owned holder state and receive readable holder/fuse feedback.
evidenceInstructions: Keep ReplicatedStorage.BombState with HolderUserId, FuseDeadline, ExplosionCount, and Status attributes; use Status values waiting, armed, and inactive.
Keep the client-to-server RemoteEvent at ReplicatedStorage.PassBomb; the server must derive the target instead of trusting its arguments.
Keep the supplied HolderMarker, NearMarker, and FarMarker parts reachable so the fixed evaluator can drive both avatars through normal movement.
Keep the visible status label at PlayerGui.BombGui.Panel.Status for the presentation capture.
